notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, and no hardware or MuJoCo run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family:ros with RosDriver, but the pinned clone is a robot-description repository, not a ROS node or control runtime. Its root README describes URDF, MuJoCo MJCF and USD descriptions (README.md:5); each description package's CMakeLists only installs the meshes, urdf, xml and world directories (HU_D03_description/CMakeLists.txt:20-30), and its manifest declares no message, service or action definition (HU_D03_description/package.xml:3-24). There is no pinned ROS endpoint, type, service or action to bind, so the card's RosDriver cannot express the repository. The package instead serves the card's models[0], HU_D03_description/xml/HU_D03_03.xml, as a configuration-only MujocoDriver: device mhs://localhost/limx-hu-d03, kind world.sim, mode simulated, risk R0. cap.world.step.v1 applies {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}} to data.ctrl and runs mj_step; cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward. The card's second model, HU_D04_description/xml/HU_D04_01.xml, is not served (one package serves one model).

MODEL AND LIMITS: the MJCF declares a free root joint and 37 hinge plus six ball joints (68 qpos, 61 qvel), 31 motors and a 0.001 s timestep (HU_D03_description/xml/HU_D03_03.xml:16, :90-403, :406-443). Every motor sets ctrllimited=true and an explicit ctrlrange; the bridge derives action.ctrl from those ctrlranges at run time (legs -120..120 / -45..45, waist -45..45, head -18..18, arms -30..30 / -18..18), refuses an out-of-range element before writing data.ctrl, and the package declares no Limit or operator-required bound of its own. The model file is read in place from the read-only clone; neither it nor its meshes are copied, imported or run.

FAKE: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's pure Python stand-in mujoco module, .fake:FakeMujoco. It parses the same MJCF for the joint dimensions, the motor ctrlranges and the timestep, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion, it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality, tendon, sensor or actuator dynamics. The model's <motor> entries are torque actuators; the stand-in's position-target interpretation is not the model's meaning. It has no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile. Nothing was compared with the real MuJoCo engine. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (model shape, per-ctrlrange refusal with zero effect, accepted boundary values, step advancing time and moving the actuated joint, step without an action, reset to the model defaults, fidelity contract, e-stop latch); all pass.

WARNINGS left by the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library, not an upstream package class the gate can wrap; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which the simulator families derive and PLAYBOOK.md section 8 treats as expected simulator-family warnings. No G4.REF_VALUE, G4.REF_BINARY or G4 reference warning was raised.

NOT COVERED: the real MuJoCo engine, its contacts, constraints and sensor dynamics; the HU_D04 model and the URDF/USD/gripper/hand variants; rendering, camera, IMU and joint-position/force/torque sensor arrays; ROS, which the clone does not provide (no node, topic, service or action); and any physical HU_D03 hardware. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no operator-required bound or driver-declared Limit exists; the control envelope is derived from the model at run time. The clone at commit 80fbd2d650c43c38916979c2a6eab7a4c79e38de was read only and is unmodified. gate.digest is the digest line of the last gate run; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the clone is a description repository: URDF, MJCF and USD files, CMakeLists that only install directories, a manifest with no interfaces, and no ROS node, topic, service or action), all 18 facts, the 31 motor ctrlranges the bridge derives its envelope from (HU_D03_03.xml:406-443), the lockstep software latch, which does stop this simulation from advancing, and the stand-in mujoco module. The fake was published with the real engine's F1 'mujoco:HU_D03_03' contract, which a test asserted; it treated the torque motors' control values as position targets (a zero torque held every joint at zero); it reset qpos to zeros, including a zero free-joint quaternion, although MuJoCo's qpos0 puts base_link at 0 0 1.0 with an identity quaternion; the CMakeLists fact cited 20-30 for a claim about the whole file; and the clone's licence notes were not recorded. The reviewer changed driver.py (fidelity keeps F1 for the real engine with shared gaps, fidelity_by_backend publishes the fake as F0 'analytic:stand-in mujoco module (no physics)' with stand-in gaps, the CMakeLists ref widened to 11-41, and facts added for the CMakeLists copyright header 'All rights reserved', the manifest's TODO licence and the README's Apache-2.0 section), fake.py (a torque-like placeholder integration and qpos0 from the MJCF), test_driver.py (the fidelity case expects F0, the reset case qpos0) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT x3) and the digest unchanged (sha256:15e765834a225a9f6b66c4a48b8e30903e0f1614372fd14c9e7b147534c1497c); the author's notes on the F1 fake contract and the position-target stand-in are superseded. For the human reviewer: The package serves the bare HU_D03 MuJoCo plant: raw torques on 31 motors (the ankle and waist motors drive rod joints closed by connect constraints) with no controller, so the humanoid falls unless a caller supplies balancing torques; reset restores qpos0 (base at 0 0 1.0). The README marks HU_D03 as discontinued and recommends HU_D04 (the card's models[1]), which is not served. No hardware path exists in the clone. Licence: README and LICENSE say Apache-2.0, while both CMakeLists files carry '© [2025] LimX Dynamics Technology Co., Ltd. All rights reserved.' and both manifests say TODO; the owner may want to confirm before publication.
